problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a convex objective over the closed ℓ₁ ball of radius R; every component is globally convex and has globally L-Lipschitz Euclidean gradient.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The objective is F(x)=(1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x), with n>0.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query selects an index i and feasible point x and returns exactly ∇fᵢ(x). No component values are supplied; replies are independent of history and oracle seed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries and outputs must satisfy ∥x∥₁≤R, while component gradient smoothness is measured in the Euclidean norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is ℝᵈ with Euclidean norm, d>0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All parameters d,n,L,R,ε are public and strictly positive. The component functions are hidden. No gradient magnitude or initial objective-gap bound is assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumNondualSmoothConvex.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: A measurable feasible output X must have integrable objective gap F(X)−F(x⋆) for a constrained minimizer x⋆.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[F(X)−F(x⋆)]≤ε under the joint algorithm and oracle randomness, with a fixed component-gradient query budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth convex finite-sum minimization over a known ℓ₁ ball with exact component-gradient access and expected objective accuracy is an established constrained optimization formulation; its constraint geometry differs from its Euclidean smoothness geometry.

descriptionHtml:
Finite-Sum Minimization on an ℓ1 Ball

We consider minimizing F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x) over C={x∈Rd:∥x∥1≤R}, where d,n are positive integers and R>0. Each component fi:Rd→R is convex and differentiable, with an L-Lipschitz gradient in the Euclidean norm, where L>0. The oracle returns ∇fi(x) at a queried component i and feasible point x∈C. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈C with integrable objective gap satisfying EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where x⋆ minimizes F on C and P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The constraint uses ∥x∥1=∑j=1d|xj|, while ∥⋅∥2 denotes the Euclidean norm. The optimization problem is minx∈CF(x). The algorithm receives d,n,L,R, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Component convexity). For every i∈{1,…,n}, every x,y∈Rd, and every t∈[0,1], fi((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)fi(x)+tfi(y).

Assumption 2 (Component smoothness). Each fi is differentiable everywhere on Rd, and ∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥2≤L∥x−y∥2,x,y∈Rd.

Oracle queries consist of a chosen index i∈{1,…,n} and a point x∈C. The smoothness and convexity conditions hold on the entire ambient space, although queries are restricted to C.

Continuity of F and compactness of C ensure that a constrained minimizer exists. Fix x⋆∈C satisfying F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈C. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must be a measurable C-valued random variable. Its objective gap must satisfy EP[|F(x¯)−F(x⋆)|]<∞,EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε.

F=n−1∑i=1nfi on Q={x∈Rd:∥x∥1≤R}, with d,n≥1 and L,R,ε>0. Each fi is globally convex, differentiable, and has an L-Lipschitz Euclidean gradient. Queries return exact component gradients at feasible points. Target: measurable x^∈Q with integrable gap and ∫[F(x^(ω))−F(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε, where x⋆∈arg⁡minQF and P is the execution law.

import LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumNondualSmoothConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  n : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero n]
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  hR : 0 ≤ R
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.nonzero

abbrev Point (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)

instance pointMeasurableSpace (d : ℕ) : MeasurableSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
  borel _

instance pointBorelSpace (d : ℕ) : BorelSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) := ⟨rfl⟩

def domain (p : Params) : Set (Point p) := {x | ∑ i, |x i| ≤ p.R}

abbrev Feasible (p : Params) := {x : Point p // x ∈ domain p}

noncomputable abbrev objective {p : Params} (f : Fin p.n → Point p → ℝ) :=
  LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.objective f

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Fin p.n → Point p → ℝ
  Query p := Fin p.n × Feasible p
  Reply p := Point p
  Output p := Feasible p
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.d ∧ 0 < p.n ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f oracle :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f i)) ∧
    (∀ i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ i x y, ‖gradient (f i) x - gradient (f i) y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ history seed i x,
      oracle.answer history (0, (i, x)) seed = gradient (f i) x.val)
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    ∃ xstar : Feasible p, IsMinOn (objective f) (domain p) xstar.val ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => objective f (output ω).val - objective f xstar.val)
        (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, objective f (output ω).val - objective f xstar.val ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumNondualSmoothConvex
